Q3 recorded and applied. Next.

**Question:** If a table file contains a completely blank line — most often one extra empty line at the very end, after the last bookmark — should the import ignore it, or fail with status 2 as a row with the wrong number of fields?

Why it matters: A blank line parses as a row holding zero fields. The spec already says a row with too few fields fails, so as written such a file is rejected — but an implementer may well add a "skip empty lines" habit, and the two behaviours need different tests. A stray trailing newline is easy for an editor to introduce.

**Recommended:** Option C - It is what the spec already says ("a row with too few or too many fields: failure code 2"), it needs no special-case code at all since the field-count check rejects an empty row on its own, and it matches constitution Principle II, which forbids skipping a record to keep running unless the spec demands it. The failure is loud and names the line, so the user can fix the file in seconds.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Ignore blank lines anywhere in the file; they are whitespace, not records. Rows with one to three or five-plus fields still fail. |
| B | Ignore blank lines only at the end of the file; a blank line between two bookmarks fails. |
| C | Fail. Any record not holding exactly four fields, including a blank line, fails with status 2 and nothing is imported. |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "C"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
